confirmed.title: v0 fused kernel _incb2_kernel inverts the store->fence->barrier order on the b_ga round-trip: GA TMA can read stale b_dv^T
confirmed.description: In _incb2_kernel's full path (bisect==0), the SIMT glue writes b_dv^T into b_ga's second half (m_bga_s, generic proxy), then executes cute.arch.barrier() BEFORE cute.arch.fence_proxy("async.global"), and warp 0 then issues the GA TMA read of m_bga (async proxy, lines 1070-1082). fence.proxy.async orders only the EXECUTING thread's prior generic accesses against subsequent async-proxy accesses; the required cross-thread pattern is store -> fence_proxy (each writing thread) -> barrier -> TMA, which is exactly what the silicon-proven siblings document and emit (gdn2_bwd_dhu_l3.py:348-355 "PTX order: stores -> fence_proxy (each writing thread) -> barrier -> TMA re-read"; gdn2_bwd_dhu_l2.py lines 242-243). With barrier-before-fence there is no synchronizes-with edge between a non-warp-0 thread's fence and warp 0's TMA issue, so the TMA can read the pre-store contents of b_ga's second half -> nondeterministically wrong t (GA output), corrupting b_dh, dh, and dh0 from that chunk backward. The acc-pipeline mbarrier does not rescue it: the phase warp 0's GA acquire (line 1065) waits on was released at line 1019, BEFORE the glue stores. The second inverted site (carry, lines 1099-1107) happens to be sequenced-safe because the NEXT chunk's dh-snapshot barrier (line 946) lands after every thread's fence. Reachability: public run_k1_incB2 (gdn2_bwd_dhu.py:1278, scalar) and gdn2_bwd_dhu_cw.run_k1_incB2 (cw) route here via _incb2_launch; the launcher-side SIGSEGV was fixed (ex(*args[:16]), line 1269) and the module's own comments say the kernel side is now unadjudicated, so this races the first time the path is exercised. Not the shipped default (L3 run_k1_incB2_v3 is), hence major not critical.

votes.reasoning: Structural facts confirmed: src/flash_mamba_rl/kernels/cute/gdn2_bwd_dhu.py:1024-1032 does SIMT stores -> cute.arch.barrier() (1030) -> cute.arch.fence_proxy("async.global") (1032) -> warp-0 GA TMA (1071-1082), inverting the fence/barrier order used by the silicon-proven L2/L3 siblings (gdn2_bwd_dhu_l3.py:354-355) and NVIDIA's own reference (scratch/refs/mamba2_ssd_v452.py:1805-1809, 2286-2291). However, the finding's load-bearing premise -- "fence.proxy.async orders only the EXECUTING thread's prior generic accesses" with "no synchronizes-with edge" -- is wrong under the governing PTX mixed-proxy memory model (Lustig et al., adopted into the PTX docs). The model's requirement, quoted verbatim in NVIDIA forum thread 358263, is: generic write X must precede the proxy fence Z in OBSERVATION ORDER (which composes through cross-thread causality, e.g. a CTA bar.sync), and Z must precede the async read Y in proxy-preserved base causality order (same-thread program order trivially qualifies). The v0 code satisfies exactly this: (1) the fence at 1031-1032 is guarded only by compile-time const_expr(bisect==0), so in the full-path build EVERY thread -- including warp 0's TMA-issuing lane -- executes barrier(1030) then fence(1032); (2) each glue store by any thread precedes warp 0's fence in observation order via the CTA-wide bar.sync (PTX barriers are morally-strong synchronization; fences are cumulative through causality); (3) warp 0's fence precedes its own TMA issue in program order. Decisively, the paper's own cross-CTA prescription (Section 5.4: the fence must be in the CTA of the async access, AFTER the sync) is only coherent if consumer-side proxy fences cover producer writes observed through synchronization -- i.e., the exact pattern v0 uses is the one the formal model prescribes in the general case; producer-side fence-before-barrier (L2/L3) and consumer-side barrier-before-fence (v0) are BOTH valid within a single CTA. Note the finding is internally inconsistent: under its own non-cumulative premise, the L2/L3 "proven" order would also be unsound (there the fence->TMA leg is cross-thread: writer's fence -> barrier -> warp 0's TMA, requiring the same fence/causality composition it claims doesn't exist). The second site (1099-1107) is likewise valid (warp 0's fence at 1107 precedes the next unrolled chunk's G1 TMA at 999+ in program order, with barrier 1105 providing the observation edge), which the finding itself concedes. Secondary context: this path is explicitly BOX-UNTESTED staging code (module comments at 821-847; run_k1_incB / L3 v3 remain the defaults) slated for a B200 micro-gate vs the fp64 oracle before any promotion, so practical exposure is nil regardless. Normalizing the order to match the siblings would be a harmless one-line consistency cleanup, not a correctness fix. Confidence is medium rather than high only because no verbatim PTX-spec sentence settling fence.proxy.async cumulativity was retrieved and this specific kernel has never run on silicon in either order; the formal-model argument, the paper's cross-CTA prescription, and the finding's internal inconsistency all point the same way: not a real bug.

The finding's scoping is also accurate: the second site (1099-1107) is rescued by the next chunk's barrier at 946 landing after every thread's fence, and the shipped default (L3 v3) is unaffected, so major (not critical) is right. Caveat: as a race it may not fire on every run (global stores often drain to L2 before TMA issue), but the code violates the pinned PTX contract on a reachable public path staged for the next silicon burst. confirmed.title: _modelled_l2 omits the f16 GMEM landings of the two GEMM outputs (bdv_raw, t_scr) that the kernels actually round-trip
confirmed.description: _modelled_l2 is documented as the kernel spec that "Includes fp16 cast round-trips for all kernel I/O (operand casts, b_ga/b_dhT stores)" and is the CPU pin (tests/test_gdn2_l2.py::test_modelled_l2_tracks_fp64_bundle, rel tol 5e-3). But the real kernels land BOTH GEMM outputs in f16 GMEM scratch before the SIMT glue reads them back: _kern_g1_epi stores the G1 accumulator to bdv_raw as f16 (line 223 tCrC.store(tCrAcc.load().to(_io))) and the glue re-reads it (line 237 m_bdv_s[bidz, r, col].to(_acc)); _kern_ga_epi does the same for t_scr (lines 373, 381). The model instead keeps both products in fp32: raw = a_g1_step @ ... (line 557) feeds b_dv un-quantized, and t = a_ga_step @ ... (line 563) feeds the carry un-quantized. Concrete consequence: the CPU test pins a numerically different (strictly more precise) path than the kernel executes, so a kernel-side regression localized to exactly these f16 landings (e.g., an epilogue dtype change) would leave the model test green; the model also cannot serve as a bit-faithful desk oracle for the L2 kernels' fp16 error accumulation over long nt chains. No wrong answer on any shipped compute path (the silicon gate grades the kernel itself vs the fp64 bundle), hence minor.

(3) The omitted quantizations (~2^-11 relative, immediately re-quantized downstream or absorbed into an fp32 carry that is already f16-quantized wholesale via the modelled b_dhT round-trip) are second-order versus the modelled effects and an order of magnitude below every tolerance in play; empirically model tracks fp64 at ~3e-4 and silicon at 7e-5, both far inside the gate. Verified line-by-line: both kernels land their GEMM outputs in f16 GMEM scratch (gdn2_bwd_dhu_l2.py:223 store to bdv_raw, :373 store to t_scr; both tensors allocated f16 at :638-639) and the SIMT glue re-reads them upcast (:237, :381), so silicon computes b_dv = f16(raw)+dvl and b_dh = glast*b_dh + f16(t). The model (_modelled_l2:557-564) keeps both products fp32, omitting exactly these two round-trips while its docstring (:521) claims fp16 round-trips are modelled for ALL kernel I/O and while every other same-class round-trip (operand casts, b_dv->b_ga store, b_dhT store) is carefully modelled and commented — so this is an oversight, not an intentional simplification. Reachability: _modelled_l2 is not on any shipped compute path (run_k1_incB_l2 never calls it); it is exercised by tests/test_gdn2_l2.py::test_modelled_l2_tracks_fp64_bundle (default CPU suite) and the scratch desk-gate harness. Impact is limited to oracle fidelity: the CPU pin certifies a strictly-more-precise path than the kernel executes, and the desk oracle understates fp16 error accumulation on the recurrent b_dh carry over long nt chains (a workflow this project relies on for zero-iteration box gates). No wrong answer ships (silicon gates grade the kernel vs the fp64 bundle directly), and a kernel epilogue-dtype regression would still be caught on box, so the claimed severity of minor is correct — but the false docstring contract plus the genuine model/kernel divergence make it a real, fixable defect rather than style or intent.

confirmed.title: FMR_DISABLE_SBE kill-switch test is a tautology: env var is never read on CPU, test compares f(x) to itself
confirmed.description:
test_closed_stage_b_torch_path_stable_under_kill_switch builds CPU fp64 tensors and compares _stage_b_vjp_cw_closed with and without FMR_DISABLE_SBE=1. But the SBE gate in gdn2_assemble.py:691-696 is `not create_graph and do.is_cuda and g2.dtype == torch.float32 and not os.environ.get("FMR_DISABLE_SBE")` — with CPU tensors `do.is_cuda` is False, so the conjunction short-circuits BEFORE `os.environ.get` executes; with fp64 the dtype gate would also fail. Both invocations therefore run byte-identical deterministic torch code, and `torch.equal` between two runs of the same deterministic CPU computation can never fail. The test's stated pin ('the env read introduces no drift') is vacuous: no env read occurs. A regression in the kill-switch wiring (e.g., the env flag accidentally inverting, or the SBE branch mutating shared state before falling back) would pass this test untouched — the kill-switch/torch-fallback parity is effectively only covered by the box-only scratch harness, which is out of the CI suite.
[dup] test_closed_stage_b_torch_path_stable_under_kill_switch is the ONLY test covering the FMR_DISABLE_SBE kill-switch (verified by grep over tests/). It calls _stage_b_vjp_cw_closed twice on identical fp64 CPU inputs, once with FMR_DISABLE_SBE=1 set, and asserts torch.equal. But in gdn2_assemble._stage_b_vjp_cw_closed the SBE gate is `not create_graph and do.is_cuda and g2.dtype == torch.float32 and not os.environ.get("FMR_DISABLE_SBE")` — on CPU the `do.is_cuda` conjunct short-circuits the expression before the env var is ever read (and the fp64 dtype would gate it off too). Both invocations therefore execute the bitwise-identical deterministic torch path; torch.equal(f(x), f(x)) cannot fail under ANY change to the kill-switch logic. Concretely: invert the condition to `os.environ.get("FMR_DISABLE_SBE")` (kill-switch becomes an enable-switch) or delete the env check entirely — this test stays green, and on a Blackwell box FMR_DISABLE_SBE=1 would route INTO the SBE kernel instead of pinning the torch fallback, which is the exact box-burst fallback the switch exists for. The docstring's own claim ("the pin is that the env read introduces no drift") is false: no env read occurs.

votes.reasoning:
The finding's mechanics are correct but its classification is not. Verified facts: in src/flash_mamba_rl/kernels/cute/gdn2_assemble.py:691-696 the gate is `not create_graph and do.is_cuda and g2.dtype == torch.float32 and not os.environ.get("FMR_DISABLE_SBE")`, and the test (tests/test_gdn2_sb_einsum.py:39-64) uses CPU fp64 tensors, so the env read is short-circuited and both calls run the identical torch path. However, this does not make the test a defective/major finding, for four reasons.

(1) Intentional, documented scope. The test module docstring (tests/test_gdn2_sb_einsum.py:3-7) explicitly says these tests "pin what is CPU-checkable" and states in so many words "(on CPU both calls take the torch path...)" and "Silicon: scratch/sbe_microgate.py + the burst-6 integration gates." The author knew both invocations take the torch fallback; kill-switch ROUTING coverage was never this test's claim. The outer docstring claim — "the closed stage-B's torch fallback stays bitwise intact under the kill-switch env" — is exactly what is asserted and is true. The finding's "docstring claim is false" hangs on the loose word "read" in a parenthetical; at most a wording nit.

(2) Not a pure tautology. The test pins env-invariance of the CPU fallback: a future change that made FMR_DISABLE_SBE perturb the torch path itself (e.g., also gating the decay_rel stash reuse or routing to a different CPU reference) would fail it. That is the only property a CPU CI can own here — the SBE kernel and its routing are unreachable off-box three gates deep (do.is_cuda False, fp32 gate, and is_available() False without cutlass per gdn2_sb_einsum.py:31-46). This suite already carries 117 CUDA-skips by design; silicon behavior is architecturally delegated to the box gate battery.

(3) The proposed regressions ARE covered where they are reachable. scratch/run_burst6.sh exercises FMR_DISABLE_SBE=1 discriminatingly on B200 (kill-fallback arm at line 60-61 and the d1 isolation arm at lines 73-77 that reruns integration with the switch set and grades GO/NOT-GO), and burst-6 silicon evidence is committed (8b312a9, "SBE kernel GO"). An inverted or deleted env check would surface there — the exact environment where the switch matters.

(4) The suggested fix is infeasible as written. The K2F pattern (tests/test_gdn2_k2_fused.py:190) transfers only because run_k2 is a selector function with no tensor.is_cuda conjunct and monkeypatchable module-level branch targets. The SBE gate is deliberately "at the wiring site" (gdn2_sb_einsum.py:21) inside _stage_b_vjp_cw_closed and conjuncts on do.is_cuda; monkeypatching is_available/run_sb_einsum with a poison stub does nothing on CPU because the env/availability checks are never reached. Making the env read reachable on CPU requires refactoring product code for testability or globally shadowing torch.Tensor.is_cuda — a design change proposal, not a bug fix.

Net: this is a test-strengthening/coverage-architecture suggestion mislabeled as a major bug. The test asserts a true, explicitly scoped property, cannot false-pass an untrue claim, and the kill-switch's discriminating behavior is verified in the project's designated silicon gates. Confidence medium rather than high because the finder's core observation (the CI suite alone cannot catch an inverted/deleted env check) is accurate; the refutation rests on the in-file documented intent and the project's box-gate testing architecture.

Executed repro confirms the tautology. Spy-patched os.environ.get and ran the test's exact call path (CPU, fp64, seed 31): FMR_DISABLE_SBE was read 0 times across both _stage_b_vjp_cw_closed invocations — the gate at gdn2_assemble.py:691-696 short-circuits at `do.is_cuda` (False on CPU) before the env clause executes, and fp64 would gate it off regardless. Both calls run byte-identical deterministic torch code, so torch.equal(f(x), f(x)) at tests/test_gdn2_sb_einsum.py:63-64 is unfalsifiable. Concrete masked-regression trigger verified: inverting the env clause (kill-switch → enable-switch) leaves the CPU gate value unchanged (False either way), so the test stays green while FMR_DISABLE_SBE=1 on a CUDA/fp32 box would route INTO the SBE kernel — the exact burst-fallback scenario (scratch/run_burst6.sh:73-75) the switch exists for. Grep confirms this is the only FMR_DISABLE_SBE test, so kill-switch wiring has zero discriminating CI coverage; the docstring's stated pin ("the env read introduces no drift") is literally vacuous since no env read occurs. This is a test-effectiveness bug, not a product-code bug — product behavior is currently correct — but the finding's claim is accurate and the suggested fix (poisoned-stub pattern mirroring test_gdn2_k2_fused.test_selector_kill_switch_and_off_tile) is the right shape.

confirmed.title: Native dispatch injects compiled kernels while create_graph follows do.requires_grad — DLPack crash instead of eager fallback
confirmed.description: native_gdn2_backward guards on device/dtype/dims but never on do.requires_grad. Downstream, assembled_channelwise_gdn2_backward (gdn2_assemble.py:994) and assembled_scalar_gdn2_backward (gdn2_assemble.py:443) set create_graph=do.requires_grad, and the assembly's detach rule `_det(t) = t if create_graph else t.detach()` (gdn2_assemble.py:353-354, 801-802) then feeds NON-detached, grad-carrying tensors (fwd.q, fwd.k, fwd.g2, ... built under grad mode by chunkwise_forward_cw) to the injected k1_fn/k2_fn. The compiled tcgen05 kernels ingest operands via DLPack (from_dlpack in gdn2_bwd_dhu*/gdn2_bwd_wy*/gdn2_sb_einsum), and torch's DLPack export refuses tensors with requires_grad=True ('Can't export tensors that require gradient'). Concrete trigger: on an sm_100 box, call ops.gdn_backward.gdn2_backward (or native_gdn2_backward / native_gla_backward / native_ssd_backward / native_kda_backward, which thread create_graph=do.requires_grad identically via gdn2_family.py:174,226,243) with a supported dtype (fp32/bf16/fp16) and do.requires_grad=True — e.g. an fp32 gradcheck of the op path on box, or any double-backward/gradient-penalty attempt. Result: RuntimeError deep in the kernel run fn instead of the documented fallback contract (return None → eager path, which handles create_graph correctly). The design docstrings only account for the fp64 create_graph case (where SUPPORTED_DTYPES makes native decline); the fp32/half create_graph case on box is unguarded. Fix keeps the invariant the code already documents: create_graph must only ever coexist with the pure-torch refs.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In native_gdn2_backward (and the four native_* family wrappers), add `if do.requires_grad: return None` (or equivalently gate on torch.is_grad_enabled() and do.requires_grad) so a double-backward request falls through to the eager path, which builds the graph correctly.

votes.reasoning: Crash mechanics are technically accurate (no requires_grad guard; _det passes grad-carrying tensors to DLPack when create_graph=True; kernel wrappers don't detach), but the path is unreachable from every caller in the repo and the finding misstates the contract. (1) The only autograd entry — _GDN2Function.backward (gdn_layer.py:99) — deliberately calls gdn2_backward with do.detach(), so no training/model/double-backward flow ever delivers a grad-requiring do to native dispatch. (2) The documented purpose of honoring do.requires_grad is CMP-02's gradcheck, which is FP64-only (contracts.py:492, the sole requires-grad caller in the verifier) and is excluded from native by two dtype gates; three docstrings frame create_graph as the fp64/pure-torch-refs path, so fp32/half create_graph on box is outside the designed input domain. (3) Caller audit: bench builds inputs without requires_grad; the family native_* wrappers have no src callers; no test or gate exercises the combination, and on-box gate batteries (incl. CMP-02) ran green. (4) native_gdn2_backward's docstring enumerates its None conditions and do.requires_grad is not one — no "documented fallback contract" is violated. (5) The proposed fix is a defensive input guard for an unproducible input, the exact "missing validation" class the project's rules exclude; and since double-backward through non-differentiable numeric tcgen05 kernels is semantically impossible, the current loud RuntimeError for a hypothetical direct on-box call is a fail-fast, not silent wrongness. At most this is a minor API-hardening suggestion, not a major bug. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the public functions are importable and a direct exotic call on silicon would genuinely crash where off-box it would not.

CONFIRMED by concrete trace + CPU repro of the exact mechanism. Trigger: on an sm_100 box, call the public op-level backward (src/flash_mamba_rl/kernels/ops/gdn_backward.py:gdn2_backward) or native_gdn2_backward / any native_* family wrapper directly with a supported dtype (fp32/bf16/fp16), conforming dims (d_k=128, L%64==0, d_v in {64,128}), and do.requires_grad=True under grad mode. native_gdn2_backward (gdn2_backward.py:144-146) guards only device/dtype/dims — no requires_grad guard — and injects the compiled kernels; assembled_channelwise_gdn2_backward (gdn2_assemble.py:994) sets create_graph=do.requires_grad, turning _det (gdn2_assemble.py:801-802) into the identity. Crucially, chunkwise_forward_cw (gdn2_chunkwise_cw.py:175-181) unconditionally rebuilds intermediates from fresh requires_grad_(True) leaves, so under grad mode EVERY fwd.* operand is grad-carrying (worse than the finding claims — not just do_c/dv_local); the compiled kernels' first act is from_dlpack(t.contiguous()) (gdn2_bwd_dhu_l3.py:94/99, l2.py:70/75, dhu.py:1195, wy_f, sb_einsum), and torch's __dlpack__ refuses grad-requiring tensors. Reproduced on CPU through the identical assembly path with stub k1_fn performing the same export: create_graph=False exports all operands cleanly; do.requires_grad=True crashes at the FIRST k1 operand (fwd.q) with BufferError 'Can't export tensors that require gradient, use tensor.detach()' (torch/_tensor.py:1760 — note: BufferError in this torch, not RuntimeError as claimed; immaterial). This violates the function's own documented fallback contract (return None -> eager, and gdn_backward.py:9-10,77-81 explicitly advertises do.requires_grad -> create_graph double-backward support on the eager path). Severity caveats: no in-repo caller reaches it today — _GDN2Function.backward detaches do (gdn_layer.py:99), and the verifier's CMP-02 gradcheck is fp64 (contracts.py:492), which SUPPORTED_DTYPES declines to eager. So it is a latent crash at the public API surface (fp32/half gradcheck on box, gradient-penalty/double-backward via the op functions, or any user Function lacking the detach), loud not silent. 'Major' is somewhat overstated; real bug nonetheless, and the suggested fix (decline native when do.requires_grad, matching the invariant the assembly comment at gdn2_assemble.py:349-354 already documents) is correct and minimal.

Every link verified in source. native_gdn2_backward (gdn2_backward.py:144-147) and _family_dims_ok guard device/dtype/dims but not do.requires_grad; the assembly wrappers set create_graph=do.requires_grad (gdn2_assemble.py:443,994; gdn2_family.py:174,226,243) and _det (:354,:668,:802,:915) then feeds non-detached operands — _det(do_c) alone, a view of do, carries requires_grad — to the injected compiled kernels, whose run fns ingest via cutlass from_dlpack (gdn2_bwd_dhu.py:510/1195 etc.). Torch's __dlpack__ refuses grad-requiring tensors, a fact the repo itself pins as an empirically-hit box fix (gdn2_assemble.py:349-352 comment). The _det create_graph no-op is only coherent for the differentiable pure-torch refs; the compiled-kernel+create_graph cell is unguarded. Reachability: this is the shipped default dispatch path — ops gdn2_backward tries native first on any CUDA fp32/half call at the shipped dims, and its docstring promises double-backward support via the eager path (gdn_backward.py:77-81, which handles it correctly). On sm_100, any grad-carrying do (gradient penalty, backward(create_graph=True), fp32 op-path gradcheck) crashes with a RuntimeError instead of the documented return-None fallback; even absent the crash, the non-differentiable kernels could never serve create_graph, so falling back is the only correct behavior. Tests miss it because all create_graph coverage is fp64 (native declines) or CPU (is_available False). Impact caveats: loud crash, not silent corruption; fires only for second-order use on box, which no in-repo loop or test exercises — a real contract violation on a public shipped API, but moderate rather than major severity. Not excused by the no-error-handling rule: dispatch guards are the design's existing mechanism and this is a missing dispatch condition. Suggested fix (return None when do.requires_grad in the five native_* wrappers) is correct and minimal.

confirmed.title: SSD half-precision grad_g is double-rounded: channel-sum taken AFTER per-channel rounding to half, violating the module's own single-round contract
confirmed.description: For fp16/bf16 inputs, _no_erase_family_backward computes all grads in fp32 but rounds them to the input half dtype before returning (gdn2_family.py:247-248). ssd_backward then produces its scalar decay grad by summing the ALREADY-ROUNDED per-channel dg over d_k (line 132: `grads[3].sum(-1)`). That is d_k(=128 on the native route) independent roundings followed by a summation, not the 'each grad rounds once at the end' contract stated in this module's docstring (lines 15-17) and honored everywhere else — kda_backward sums db/dw in fp32 first and rounds the result once (lines 176-184). Concrete failure: with cross-channel cancellation (per-channel dg components O(1) summing to O(1e-2)), the per-channel half roundings (~5e-4 abs each in fp16, ~4e-3 in bf16) accumulate into an error on grad_g that can exceed the true value's magnitude, where the single-round path would be exact to one ulp of the sum. Reachable on the shipped native SSD family route (native_ssd_backward with bf16/fp16 on box) and on the desk torch path.
confirmed.evidence: gdn2_family.py:247-248: `if half:\n        dq, dk, dv, dg = (t.to(in_dtype) for t in (dq, dk, dv, dg))` then gdn2_family.py:132: `return SsdGrads(grad_q=grads[0], grad_k=grads[1], grad_v=grads[2], grad_g=grads[3].sum(-1))` — contrast kda_backward gdn2_family.py:181: `grad_beta=grads.db.sum(-1) + grads.dw.sum(-1),` computed on fp32 grads BEFORE the single half round at line 184.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Perform the channel reduction before the half round: either have ssd_backward do the .sum(-1) on the fp32 dg (e.g. let _no_erase_family_backward return fp32 grads plus the in_dtype, or move the SSD sum inside the helper pre-round), mirroring kda_backward's order.

votes.reasoning: Mechanics confirmed (gdn2_family.py:247-248 rounds dg to half, line 132 sums after; kda_backward sums fp32 first), but the bug claim does not hold up. (1) Contract: the module docstring defines wrappers as assembly + grad mapping ("channel-sum what it holds scalar"), and its mixed-precision sentence delegates to assembled_channelwise_gdn2_backward's contract, which governs the six ASSEMBLY grads — each of which does round once. SSD grad_g is a mapped quantity; extending "rounds once" to it is the finding's interpretation, not the documented contract. KDA's opposite order is structural (it cannot use the shared helper), not proof of intent for SSD. (2) No pinned expectation is violated: family value tests are fp64-only; the verifier's family gate battery uses this same wrapper as its structurally-matched reference (op_harness.py:1428-1452), so the shipped sum-after-round behavior IS the pinned behavior; the silicon family credential runs fp32; full suite passes. (3) The failure scenario relies on element-relative accuracy under cross-channel cancellation — a criterion the project's scale-aware error model (scale_atol_by_ref_inf, _scale_rel gates, rationale documented in op_harness) explicitly rejects. Under scale_rel the added error (~sqrt(d_k)*0.5ulp of per-channel magnitude, ~1e-3 of tensor scale in bf16 at d_k=128) sits inside PRC-02's 2e-3 atol, the 5e-3 silicon gate, and the tcgen05 kernels' own accepted ~3.3e-3 error on the same route; bf16 native family credentials and 300-step training ran GO with this ordering live. Residual: a real but cosmetic SSD/KDA ordering inconsistency (sum-first is marginally better and a one-line change), which is why confidence is medium rather than high — it is a polish candidate, not a correctness defect.

Reproduced concretely on CPU via the shipped desk path (same code the native route hits: src/flash_mamba_rl/kernels/cute/gdn2_backward.py:249 native_ssd_backward -> ssd_backward; the half round at gdn2_family.py:247-248 fires regardless of k1_fn). Exact trigger: ssd_backward with bf16 inputs, B=1, L=128, H=2, d_k=128, d_v=64, q/k/v/do ~ N(0,1), g ~ -U(0,0.01) (torch.manual_seed(1)), defaults (fast_path=True, use_qk_l2norm=True). Method: quantize inputs to bf16 once, then compare (a) shipped grad_g (per-channel dg rounded to bf16 at gdn2_family.py:248, then .sum(-1) at line 132) vs (b) the contract order (same fp32 computation, fp32 sum over d_k, single round to bf16) vs (c) fp64 truth on the identical quantized inputs. Results: shipped != single-round at 101-223 of 256-512 positions, up to 215 bf16 ulps apart; at non-degenerate positions (|truth| > 5% of median magnitude) shipped max relative error on grad_g is 6.4e-2 to 9.5e-2 across four seeds/regimes, while the single-round order stays at 3.5e-3 to 3.8e-3 (i.e. the one-final-round guarantee) — a ~20-25x rel-error inflation; mean abs error 1.6-2.4x worse. Concrete instance: truth=2.827174, single-round=2.828125 (1 ulp), shipped=2.843750 (0.59% off, several ulps). No engineered cancellation needed — generic partial cancellation among 128 signed per-channel dg components suffices (the finding's extreme 'error exceeds truth magnitude' variant occurred only at 3/256 near-zero-truth positions with random data, so that specific phrasing needs constructed inputs, but the core defect manifests generically). This violates the module docstring's stated mixed-precision contract (gdn2_family.py:15-17, 'each grad rounds once at the end') which kda_backward honors (fp32 db.sum(-1)+dw.sum(-1) at line 181 before the single round at line 184); ssd_backward at line 132 is the lone violator. Severity 'minor' is apt: correct math, degraded numerics on one returned grad, plus an internal-contract inconsistency; the suggested fix (sum the fp32 dg before the half round) matches the verified kda ordering.

Confirmed by code read and empirical repro. gdn2_family.py:247-248 rounds dg per-channel to the input half dtype, then ssd_backward line 132 sums the already-rounded dg over d_k — violating the module docstring's own single-round contract (lines 15-17) that kda_backward honors for the identical scalar-gate reduction (fp32 sum at line 181, one round at line 184). Repro on the desk path (b1/L64/h2/dk128, plain random inputs): shipped grad_g differs from the single-round value at ~46% of positions; rounding-order error mean 1.15/max 15.6 ulps (bf16) and mean 22.5/max ~2170 ulps (fp16) vs the <=0.5 ulp single-round achieves; unbounded relative error under cross-channel cancellation. Reachable on shipped paths: native_ssd_backward (gdn2_backward.py:235-249) dispatches bf16/fp16 (SUPPORTED_DTYPES) directly into ssd_backward on the box, and the verifier op_harness maps "ssd" to it. Tests pass only because family value tests run fp64 (half branch never taken) and the gate battery compares against a structurally matched wrapper. Impact is bounded (half precision only, one grad, few-to-thousands of ulps), so severity "minor" is correct, but it is a genuine violation of an explicit numerical-correctness invariant in a project whose contribution is verified contracts — not style or intentional design. Suggested fix (sum fp32 dg before the single round, mirroring kda_backward) is correct.

confirmed.title: Memory-blind default scan-mode gate dispatches long-L backward to chunk_parallel whose scratch guard aborts, where serial computes fine
confirmed.description: With config=None (the shipped default), `_default_scan_mode` sends every backward with seq_len>4096 (and most others) to chunk_parallel, whose recompute scratch is O(B*L*D*block_n) fp32 — at the Mamba-3 state size n_state=128 (block_n=128, explicitly supported: MAX_BLOCK_N=128 and the _BWD_TILE_BUDGET block_d shrink exist for exactly this), that is 512 bytes per (b,l,d) element, 32-64x the activation size. The launcher then raises ValueError when hbuf exceeds 0.7*free VRAM (_triton_chunk_parallel_bwd.py:315-322; identical guard in _triton_chunk_parallel_fused_bwd.py:484-491). Concrete failure: backward_selective_scan(u[8,16384,2048], A[2048,128], config=None) on the repo's own B200-192GB — gate returns 'chunk_parallel' (16384>4096 so both serial rules miss), _auto_chunk_len gives 512, block_n=128, block_d=16, n_d_blocks=128, hbuf_elems=8*32*128*512*16*128=3.44e10 -> 137.4 GB > 0.7*~185 GB free -> ValueError raised inside loss.backward() (via _ForwardScanCuda.backward or the public backward_selective_scan). The serial kernel handles this exact shape in ~30 GB of scratch (gb/gc partials 8.6 GB each + ckpt 8.6 GB), so a computable default-path training backward becomes a hard failure. Same defect reachable through fused_block_backward / _FusedBlockCuda.backward (same _resolve_scan_mode gate, same guard). The chunk-parallel module's own contract claim is violated: _triton_chunk_parallel_bwd.py:34-36 says 'At small-batch/long-L (the regime this targets) this is a few GB and fits; the mode selector / autotuner only picks it where it does' — true only at n_state=16; the selector consults shape (seq_len, batch, width) but never n_state or available memory, and there is no serial fallback when the guard trips.
confirmed.evidence: forward_chunked_scan.py:83-89: `if is_forward and seq_len <= 512: return "serial"` / `if batch >= 8 and width >= 4096 and seq_len <= 4096: return "serial"` / `if batch >= 8 and width >= 2048 and seq_len <= 512: return "serial"` / `return "chunk_parallel"` — no n_state or memory term. _triton_chunk_parallel_bwd.py:315-322: `hbuf_elems = batch * n_chunks * n_d_blocks * chunk_len * block_d * block_n` ... `if hbuf_elems * 4 > 0.7 * free_bytes: raise ValueError(f"chunk_parallel backward scratch ~{...} GB exceeds {...} GB free; use serial scan_mode or smaller chunk_len")` — raises instead of falling back to the serial kernel that the very same dispatcher owns.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the default gate memory-aware: in _resolve_scan_mode (or at the dispatch sites), when scan_mode is unset compute the chunk-parallel scratch estimate (batch * seq_len * d_model_rounded * block_n * 4 bytes) and fall back to 'serial' when it exceeds the guard threshold — reserving the hard ValueError for an explicit config.scan_mode=='chunk_parallel' request (where honest failure is the intended config-scoring behavior). Alternatively catch the guard at the dispatch sites and reroute config-None calls to the serial launcher.

votes.reasoning: Tried to refute; every element of the finding verified against the code instead. (1) The default gate (forward_chunked_scan.py:83-89) consults only (seq_len, batch, width) and returns chunk_parallel for backward at b8/L16384/d2048 — this exact tuple is test-pinned at tests/test_scan_mode_selector.py:47. (2) At n_state=128 (explicitly supported and tuned: MAX_BLOCK_N=128, _BWD_TILE_BUDGET comment citing bwd_n128_sweep), the launcher computes hbuf = 8*32*128*512*16*128 elems = 137.4 GB, and the guard at _triton_chunk_parallel_bwd.py:315-322 raises ValueError whenever hbuf > 0.7*free — which trips even on a completely empty 192 GB B200 (max threshold 134.4 GB). (3) No fallback: backward_selective_scan.py:83-91 and _ForwardScanCuda.backward call the launcher bare; no except anywhere in src. (4) The forward chunk_parallel launcher has no O(B*L*D*N) scratch, so training succeeds through forward and hard-fails inside loss.backward(). (5) The serial backward handles the shape (~30 GB: chunk_k-capped ckpt + 8.6 GB gb/gc partials). (6) The guard message's remedy 'smaller chunk_len' is mathematically inert — hbuf contains n_chunks*chunk_len = L so it is chunk_len-invariant; only serial works, and the gate never picks it on memory grounds. (7) The module's own docstring (_triton_chunk_parallel_bwd.py:34-36) promises the selector only picks chunk_parallel where the scratch fits — a contract the shape-only selector cannot honor; the calibration sweep JSON has no n_state field. (8) No test covers the guard (no mem_get_info/message reference in tests). Refutation angles rejected: not out-of-scope (n128 tuned for), not intentional for config=None (the honest-failure rationale applies to explicit config scoring), not the project's no-error-handling ethos (validation exists; the bug is the dispatch policy), not unreachable (trips on the project's own B200 at empty-GPU state, and the failing region grows under normal memory pressure, eventually including n_state=16 shapes). Mitigation: failure is loud and actionable, never silent corruption — but a default-path training backward that deterministically raises where the sibling serial kernel computes fine, at a regime the library advertises, is a real defect; 'major' is defensible for a kernels library.

Trace confirmed end-to-end with exact arithmetic. Trigger: backward_selective_scan(u[8,16384,2048] fp32 CUDA, A[2048,128], config=None) on a 192GB B200. (1) _default_scan_mode (forward_chunked_scan.py:83-89) with is_forward=False returns 'chunk_parallel' for seq_len=16384 (both serial rules require seq_len<=4096/512); the gate consults only seq_len/batch/width, never n_state or memory. (2) backward_selective_scan.py:83-91 dispatches to launch_backward_chunk_parallel_scan with chunk_len=_auto_chunk_len(16384,None)=512; no try/except in any caller (also verified _ForwardScanCuda.backward and fused_block_backward). (3) Launcher (_triton_chunk_parallel_bwd.py:299-322): block_n=128 (n_state=128 explicitly supported, MAX_BLOCK_N=128), block_d=16, n_d_blocks=128, hbuf_elems=8*32*128*512*16*128=3.436e10 -> 137.4 GB, which exceeds 0.7*free_bytes for EVERY possible free value on a 192GB device (0.7*192=134.4 GB), so the ValueError at lines 319-322 raises unconditionally inside loss.backward(). (4) The serial kernel (_triton_bwd_scan.py) passes its own MAX_BLOCK_N=128 check at this shape and needs only ~26-30 GB scratch (gb/gc partials 8.59 GB each + ckpt ~8.6 GB), so the shape is computable via the dispatcher's own sibling kernel. The module docstring's claim that 'the mode selector only picks it where it fits' (lines 34-36) is unimplemented — no memory/n_state term exists. Failure surface widens under real training memory pressure (free_bytes dynamic): e.g. b=2/L=16384/D=2048/N=128 (34.4 GB scratch) trips whenever free<~49 GB. Not shielded by the project's no-error-handling invariant: the defect is the default dispatch policy deterministically routing to a kernel that aborts where the serial kernel computes, not missing validation. Only caveat: not executed on silicon (no local GPU), but every quantity in the failure path except free_bytes is pure shape arithmetic (replicated and verified by execution), and the trip condition holds for all free_bytes values on the stated hardware.

Verified end-to-end in source. (1) _default_scan_mode (forward_chunked_scan.py:83-89) keys only on seq_len/batch/width; every backward with seq_len>4096 under config=None resolves to chunk_parallel. (2) config=None is the shipped default at all four dispatch sites (_ForwardScanCuda.backward, backward_selective_scan, fused_block_forward/backward). (3) The chunk-parallel launcher guard (_triton_chunk_parallel_bwd.py:315-322; twin at _triton_chunk_parallel_fused_bwd.py:484-491) raises ValueError with no serial fallback. (4) Arithmetic checks out: b8/L16384/d2048/N128 gives chunk_len=512, block_n=128, block_d=16, n_d_blocks=128, hbuf=3.44e10 elems=137.4 GB > 0.7*~185 GB free on the project's B200-192GB, so a default-path loss.backward() hard-fails on a shape the serial kernel computes in ~30 GB; on the fleet's H100-80GB even n_state=64 shapes (b8/L8192/d4096 = 68.7 GB) trip it. (5) The module's own contract (_triton_chunk_parallel_bwd.py:34-36, 'the mode selector only picks it where it fits') is violated: the calibration sweep (scratch/scan_mode_boundary.py + results/scan_mode_boundary.json) never varied n_state (effectively N=16, 8x smaller scratch), and the selector has no memory/n_state term. Reachability: currently-exercised paths dodge it (PTB-XL is L~1000/d_state=64 and lands serial; C2 bench shapes are all N=16; desk tests CUDA-skip), which is why the suite is green — but n_state=128 is the Mamba-3 default the project explicitly engineered for (MAX_BLOCK_N=128, _BWD_TILE_BUDGET shrink, bwd_n128_sweep, head-to-head bench), so this sits on the shipped default dispatch for exactly the long-L Mamba-3 regime the kernels target. Not the intentional no-error-handling design: the guard's honest raise is fine for explicit config scoring, but the memory-blind default gate routing a computable shape into a launcher that provably cannot run it, with no fallback, is a functional dispatch defect. Real bug on a reachable default path; severity major-but-regime-limited (requires long L + large B*D*n_state relative to GPU memory).

confirmed.title: _parse_module_attrs lets ast.literal_eval TypeError escape, crashing candidate discovery on a degenerate candidate file
confirmed.description: The per-node handler only catches (ValueError, SyntaxError), but ast.literal_eval also raises TypeError for syntactically valid literals with unhashable container keys/elements. Verified on the repo's Python 3.14: `X = {[]: 1}` -> TypeError "cannot use 'list' as a dict key"; `Y = {{}}` -> TypeError "cannot use 'dict' as a set element". A single RL-generated/degenerate candidate file containing such a module-level assignment makes load_candidate() raise TypeError, and because discover_candidates() (loader.py:157) loads every kernel_*.py eagerly, one bad file aborts the entire sweep's discovery instead of that candidate simply losing its metadata. This contradicts the function's own contract and existing handling: the docstring says it "Skips anything that requires execution", it already returns {} on module-level SyntaxError (loader.py:62-64) and skips per-node ValueError, so the exception set is incomplete rather than error handling being absent. confirmed.title: MIMO SFT triton kernel dropped the int64 promotion of the checkpoint tile offset that its production twin carries
confirmed.description: In _mimo_bwd_kernel the per-chunk checkpoint offset is computed as `c * BLOCK_P * BLOCK_N` with `c` an int32 loop induction variable (line 108 store, line 139 load). The production kernel this file is documented to mirror (src/flash_mamba_rl/kernels/ops/_triton_mimo_bwd.py lines 137 and 168) promotes exactly this product via `c.to(tl.int64)`, with a comment noting it crosses 2^31 once the per-program ckpt region exceeds 8 GiB; the C2 and fused-backward SFT siblings (backward_selective_scan_triton.py:93,125; fused_block_backward_triton.py:124,285) all carry the promotion. Concrete failure path: mimo_backward on CUDA with batch=1, nheads=1, headdim in (65,128] (BLOCK_P=128), n_state >= 64 (BLOCK_N=64), seq_len >= 16*(2^18+1) (~4.19M) gives n_chunks > 2^18, the launcher successfully allocates the ~8.6 GB ckpt scratch on a B200, and at c >= 2^18 the int32 product wraps negative; the checkpoint store is an unmasked full-tile store, so the kernel writes ~8 GB below its scratch region (silent corruption of other allocations or an illegal-address fault), and the mirrored load at line 139 reads garbage state, corrupting every gradient of the affected chunks. confirmed.title: benchmark() silently times GPU closures with the unsynchronized CPU wall-clock — every bench/* module measures host enqueue, not device time
confirmed.description: Commit 61e0af4 (2026-07-01) changed timer selection from `use_cuda = torch.cuda.is_available()` to probing the positional inputs for CUDA tensors. Every bench harness in src/flash_mamba_rl/bench (c1..c6, mamba3_backward_headtohead.py:127, gdn2_backward_headtohead.py:99) calls `benchmark(fn, ())` with the CUDA tensors captured in a closure, so `probe = ()`, `any(...)` over an empty tuple is False, and `use_cuda` is False on a CUDA box. The timed loop then runs `t0 = perf_counter_ns(); callable(); t1` with NO torch.cuda.synchronize anywhere in the timed window (and none between warmup and trials), so each trial records only host-side enqueue time for async CUDA work (Triton launches, torch.autograd.grad, selective_scan_fn). Concrete failure path: on the B200, `python -m flash_mamba_rl.bench.gdn2_backward_headtohead` — `_bench_ours`'s closure happens to sync internally (maybe_sync inside the CuTe run fns) and gets roughly-real device time, while `_bench_fla`/`_bench_cula`'s autograd.grad closures return right after enqueue, so `fla_over_ours`/`cula_over_ours` compare device time against launch overhead and are invalid; in c1-c6 and mamba3_backward_headtohead BOTH sides are enqueue-timed and the derived achieved_tflops/mfu are meaningless. Any bench/* rerun after 2026-07-01 (e.g. the burst-6 final-campaign re-bench) produced these invalid GPU medians; before 61e0af4 these callers correctly took the CUDA-event path with a per-trial sync. The verifier reward path (op_bench.measure_speedup) is unaffected — it passes inputs_factory yielding real CUDA tensors, so the probe sees them.
confirmed.evidence: timing.py:67-70: `probe = call_inputs(-1)` / `use_cuda = torch.cuda.is_available() and any(isinstance(a, torch.Tensor) and a.is_cuda for a in probe)`; fallback branch timing.py:91-96: `t0 = time.perf_counter_ns(); callable(*args); t1 = time.perf_counter_ns()` (no synchronize). Callers: gdn2_backward_headtohead.py:99 `r = benchmark(fn, (), warmup=warmup, trials=trials)`; c1_forward_chunked_scan.py:91 `result = benchmark(fn, (), warmup=warmup, trials=trials)`; mamba3_backward_headtohead.py:127 same.

Re-run any bench/* artifacts generated after 2026-07-01.

confirmed.description: assemble_gdn2_backward_scalar detaches the K#2 kernel operands via _det() (lines 353-368, with the DLPack rationale comment), but the very next statement calls _k2_beta_split with the raw fwd.k/fwd.v/fwd.beta/fwd.g2/fwd.T. chunkwise_forward builds these as grad-carrying non-leaf tensors rooted at fresh leaves (gdn2_chunkwise.py:155-160, docstring 'Tensors carry grad history'). The scalar backward always executes with grad mode ON (_GDN2Function.backward wraps gdn2_backward in torch.enable_grad() at gdn_layer.py:91, and direct verifier calls run under default grad-enabled mode because the assembly's autograd stage B requires it), so even when create_graph is False the _k2_beta_split outputs db_erase/dw_write acquire grad_fn. They flow unbroken through assembled_scalar_gdn2_backward's expand/divide/.contiguous()/.to(in_dtype) into Gdn2Grads.grad_b/grad_w. Trigger: any backward through the shipped scalar-reducible native route (b == w == beta*1, g channel-constant, d_k=128, d_v=64, L%64==0 on sm_100), or any grad-enabled call of assembled_scalar_gdn2_backward with do.requires_grad False. Wrong behavior: after loss.backward() the b/w parameter .grad tensors have requires_grad=True and keep the full scalar chunkwise-forward graph (per-chunk T solves, h_list state chain, A_qk) alive until .grad is overwritten - a create_graph=False backward is contractually supposed to return graph-free grads; any later differentiable arithmetic on those grads (e.g. grad-penalty or clipping math executed outside no_grad) silently differentiates into the backward's internal recompute instead of treating the gradient as a constant. Reproduced concretely on CPU (uv run, fp32, B=1/T=64/H=1/d_k=8/d_v=4, scalar regime, do.requires_grad=False => create_graph=False): assembled_scalar_gdn2_backward returns grad_b/grad_w with requires_grad=True and grad_fn=<DivBackward0>, while grad_q/k/v/g are graph-free and the channel-wise crown path returns graph-free grad_b/grad_w — confirming gdn2_assemble.py:370 feeds _k2_beta_split the raw graph-carrying fwd.k/v/beta/g2/T (built from requires_grad_(True) leaves in gdn2_chunkwise.py:155-160) instead of the _det()-detached operands used one line above for k2(). This is exactly the asymmetry the finding names, and _k2_beta_split is pure torch so nothing (unlike DLPack for the kernels) rejects the grad-carrying inputs on the real sm_100 route either. Exact triggers verified: (a) the verifier's direct call (op_harness.py:1177) and any grad-enabled call — returned Gdn2Grads retains the chunkwise-forward subgraph (T solves etc.) while grad_b/grad_w live; (b) torch.autograd.grad(loss, (b, w)) with create_graph=False through a Function.backward wrapped in torch.enable_grad() (the gdn_layer.py:91 pattern) returns grads with requires_grad=True and live grad_fn — a create_graph=False contract violation where later differentiable arithmetic on the grads silently differentiates into the backward's internal recompute. One sub-claim is overstated: after plain loss.backward(), leaf b/w .grad tensors come out requires_grad=False (AccumulateGrad detaches on the steal path / clones under grad-mode-off), so the specific ".grad keeps the graph alive until overwritten" scenario does not manifest on current torch; in realistic models b/w grads also pass through further backward nodes executed under no-grad, which strips the graph. Net: real, correctly-diagnosed minor bug with a correct one-line fix (route _k2_beta_split operands through _det()), matching the claimed minor severity.
